# build.sh: data/sales.csv -> dist/summary.txt (region totals, biggest first,
# ties by region name).
# Contract: if any stage fails, build.sh exits non-zero and dist/summary.txt
# is left exactly as it was. FAIL_STAGE=<stage> injects a failure into that
# stage (extract, transform, validate, publish); the tests rely on it.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

stage() {
  if [ "${FAIL_STAGE:-}" = "$1" ]; then
    echo "injected failure in $1" >&2

  fi

extract() {
  local rows=$(stage extract && grep -v '^#' data/sales.csv | cut -d, -f2,3)

transform() {
  stage transform
  awk -F, '{ total[$1] += $2 } END { for (r in total) print r "," total[r] }' \

validate() {
  stage validate
  if grep -qv '^[a-z][a-z]*,[0-9][0-9]*$' build/totals.csv; then

    awk -F, '{ printf "%-6s %5d\n", $1, $2 }' > dist/summary.txt
}

main() {
  extract
  if ! transform; then
    echo "transform failed, continuing with previous totals" >&2

}

#!/bin/bash
# publish SRC DEST: render the key=value file SRC into DEST as "key: value"
# lines sorted by key (LC_ALL=C byte order). Blank lines and lines starting
# with # are ignored. Every line of SRC counts, even a last line without a
# trailing newline. Values may contain "=".
#
# Contract (tests/test_publish.sh checks all of it):
#   exit 0  success: DEST replaced, nothing printed on stdout
#   exit 2  usage error (not exactly two arguments)
#   exit 3  SRC has a line that is not blank, not a comment and not
#           key=value with key matching [a-z_]+ ; prints
#           "publish: bad line N" (N = 1-based line number) on stderr
#   exit 4  the directory DEST would be written to does not exist
#   On every non-zero exit DEST is left untouched, and on every exit no
#   temporary file or directory remains in ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}.
set -eu

[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "usage: publish SRC DEST" >&2; exit 1; }
src=$1 dest=$2

render() {
  local tmp=$(mktemp)
  local work=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
  n=0
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    case $line in
      ''|'#'*) continue ;;
      [a-z_]*=*) echo "$line" >> "$work/pairs" ;;
      *) echo "publish: bad line $n" >&2; exit 3 ;;
    esac
  done < "$src"
  sort "$work/pairs" | sed 's/=/: /' > "$tmp"
  cp "$tmp" "$dest"
}

render
trap 'echo "publish: done"; exit 0' EXIT

description: 12000-line generated access log: route normalisation, nearest-rank p50/p95, half-up error %, malformed count

Group valid lines by method and normalised path: drop the query string, drop one trailing '/' (except for the root path '/'), and replace every path segment made only of digits with `:id`. Write /out/endpoints.tsv (tab-separated) with header method, path, count, p50, p95, error_pct, sorted by count descending, then method, then path; error_pct always printed with 1 decimal. Write /out/malformed.txt with just the number of malformed lines.

methods = ['GET', 'GET', 'GET', 'POST', 'DELETE', 'GET', 'PUT']
